title: Factory foundations
description: The blocking prerequisites from docs/design/cloud-factory.md before any factory code: the self-contained cloud/factory/ worker bundle (current compatibility date, R2 binding), single-tenant secrets-not-accounts auth (D16), the tk factory deploy / tk factory setup install story, and retiring the vestigial ralph/swarm enum from the run_event schema. Deliberately excludes RunRoom, Workflows, and sandboxes — those are Phase 1.

2026-08-19 15:58 - gotcha for the retro (tk 0.30.0): 'tk update <id> --blocked-by <other>' silently accepts the flag and changes nothing — exit 0, no warning, blocked_by untouched. Adding a blocker after creation requires 'tk block <id> <blocker...>'. --blocked-by only works on 'tk create'. 2026-08-19 16:01 - CORRECTION to the previous note: there is NO tk bug. 'tk update <id> --blocked-by <other>' fails loudly and correctly — 'Error: unknown flag: --blocked-by', exit 2, tick untouched — because --blocked-by is registered only on createCmd. My earlier 'silent no-op' claim was an artefact of my own shell hygiene: I piped the command through '2>&1 | tail -1', which discarded the error and the exit code and left a blank line that I read as success. Do not promote the previous note to learnings. The real, transferable lesson is the orchestration one: never pipe a tracker-mutating command through head/tail — you throw away exactly the diagnostics that tell you the mutation did not happen. Check exit status explicitly, and verify the mutation by re-reading state.
